findings.claim: The Katha Upanishad 2.2.6-8 describes Brahman as subtler than the subtlest, greater than the greatest, the self of all beings.
findings.truth: That line is Katha Upanishad 1.2.20 ('smaller than the small, greater than the great'). Katha 2.2.6-8 gives the secret eternal Brahman, rebirth according to karma, and the self that is awake while we sleep, in which all the worlds rest.
findings.evidence: spec 2E section 1.1 names Katha Upanishad 2.2.6-8; Wikipedia, Katha Upanishad (verse 1.2.20; Fifth Valli summary)

findings.claim: [0].marks credits 'described in the Upanishads (Katha Upanishad 2.2.6-8) as subtler than the subtlest'.
findings.truth: Same misattribution as F1; the mark scheme would credit a wrong reference.

findings.claim: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad definition: '4.4 discusses kamma and rebirth'.
findings.truth: Kamma is the Pali (Buddhist) spelling. The Hindu Sanskrit term, used everywhere else in the unit, is karma.

findings.claim: 'anatana dharma (eternal law)' is taught as the term, in content, conclusion, exam tip, flashcard 10 and glossary 10.
findings.truth: The term is sanatana dharma (Sanskrit: eternal dharma). 'Anatana' is not a Sanskrit word; the specification prints it once as a typographical error at section 1.6. The exam tip currently tells students to spell the non-word for SPaG credit. Fixed to sanatana dharma, with the spec's printed form flagged once in the exam tip.
findings.evidence: spec 2E section 1.6 (single occurrence, no other board or textbook usage); standard Sanskrit

findings.claim: Bhagavad Gita 6.44-47 is presented as the source for karma yoga.
findings.truth: 6.44-47 sits in the meditation chapter and closes by exalting the devotee (6.47). The spec cites it under 2.1 for Hindu yoga as a whole and under 2.4 for prayer, so a student who names it for yoga is still on spec; only the pairing with karma yoga is loose.

findings.claim: The definition glosses 'Lead us from darkness to light' as (asato ma sad gamaya).
findings.truth: Asato ma sad gamaya means 'from the unreal to the real'. 'From darkness to light' is tamaso ma jyotir gamaya.

findings.claim: The quotation reads 'Lead us from darkness to light, from the unreal to the real, from death to immortality'.
findings.truth: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.3.28 runs: from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.

findings.claim: Varanasi, Vrindavana and the Ganges are 'three distinct types of pilgrimage: to a sacred river, to a sacred city and to a deity's birthplace'.
findings.truth: Krishna was born at Mathura, not Vrindavana. Vrindavana is where he spent his childhood, as the same lesson says two sentences earlier.
findings.evidence: spec 2E section 2.6; standard account of Krishna's birth at Mathura

findings.claim: Rig Veda 10.75 'praises the sacred rivers of India, especially the Ganges'.
findings.truth: The Nadistuti sukta is addressed chiefly to the Sindhu (Indus), named in verses 1, 2, 7, 8 and 9. The Ganga is named once, heading the list of ten rivers in verse 5.

findings.claim: 'the spec names eight festivals'.
findings.truth: The spec lists seven items: Diwali, Holi, 'Navratri Dussehra' (printed without a comma), Ram Navami, Ratha-yatra, Janmashtami and Raksha Bandhan. Treating Navratri and Dussehra as two is defensible, so no edit.

findings.truth: House limit is under 100 characters. Not a factual error, so left alone.

summary: Doctrine, deities, festivals, pilgrimage and every knowledge-check answer key are sound. The damage is in scripture attribution (Katha Upanishad 2.2.6-8 given the words of 1.2.20; asato ma sad gamaya glossed as the wrong line and the 1.3.28 prayer reordered), one wrong pilgrimage claim (Vrindavana as Krishna's birthplace), one Pali spelling (kamma) and the spec's 'anatana dharma' typo carried into teaching text; plus a repeated exam-form error in all four lessons - a 3-mark Describe question, which the spec sets at 4 marks, and the 12-mark question written in another board's Discuss form instead of Evaluate.
